about: The facts planted in the legacy-billing fixture and how score.py recognises them in a document repository. An anchor names a file of the fixture and the text of its first line (`match`), optionally the text of its last line (`through`, the first line at or after `match` that contains it); citations within `slack` lines of the range count as citing it (dead code is matched exactly, so a rule of the paragraph before it is not counted).

rules.fact: A gold customer (tier G) gets 10% off the subtotal; every other customer gets none.
Shipping is free when the subtotal is over 1000.00 and 25.00 otherwise.
Tax is the discounted subtotal times the rate of the order's region, looked up in TAXTAB, whose source is missing.
An order more than 30 days overdue pays 2% of the subtotal per full month late, capped at 50.00.
A customer id is valid when it is C followed by seven digits; otherwise the result is 10.
An order is refused (result 20) when the customer's balance plus the order amount exceeds the credit limit.
An order whose customer is not on the master file is rejected with reason 30.
An order that fails validation is written to the reject file with its order id and reason, and is not priced.

gaps.fact: Copybook TAXTAB is copied by INVCALC but is not in the repository: the tax regions and rates are unknown.
INVBATCH calls the program named in the control file (CTLFILE, dataset BILL.PROD.CONTROL(INVOUT)), which is not provided: the callee is unknown.
The comment says gold customers get 5% but the code gives 10%.

findings.fact: CUSTVAL connects to the database with a password written in the source.

unmarkedClaims.fact: Nothing in the source shows that INVBATCH calls INVPRT; a specification of INVBATCH that names INVPRT must mark it.

deadCode.fact: Paragraph 9000-HOLIDAY-PROMO is never performed; a rule drawn from it must say so.
